title: Baroque Style

sections.title: Baroque Style: Ornament, Continuo, and Dance

blocks.text: Baroque music (c. 1600–1750) features continuous motion, basso continuo, expected ornamentation, and dance-suite organisation.
Keyboard and lute realise harmonies from a bass line with figured-bass numbers. Melody instruments play above this foundation.
Trills, mordents, appoggiaturas expected — especially on cadences and repeats. Baroque treatises (Quantz, C.P.E. Bach) document practice.
Allemande, courante, sarabande, gigue — court dances structuring instrumental music. O'Carolan and baroque flute arrangements inhabit this world.

quiz_markdown:
### Q1. Basso continuo:

- A) Bass line with harmonic figures realised by keyboard
- B) Capo on fret 2
- C) Solo whistle
- D) Percussion only

**Answer:** A

### Q2. Ornamentation was expected in baroque performance.

**Answer:** True
